I farm in Quzhou County, Hebei, so I will follow the usual pattern that fits my land, water, and labor best: a winter wheat and summer maize rotation. That is the most reliable way for me to keep the land productive across the full year. At the start of the growing season, I will already have winter wheat in the field or I will center my whole year around getting wheat harvested and then sowing summer maize right after. I will not spread myself across many crops, because at my age I want a system I know well, can manage on time, and can sell easily. Wheat and maize are the crops I trust most for stable grain output in my area.

For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed instead of old saved seed because I want better stand establishment, better resistance, and more dependable yield. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage where it helps me save labor and finish field work quickly, especially before sowing maize after wheat. For fertilizer, I will use moderate but solid nutrient rates. Wheat needs enough nitrogen for tillering and grain filling, along with phosphorus and potassium for rooting and plant strength. Maize also needs strong nitrogen support, but I will still apply phosphorus and potassium so the crop does not go weak later. I will split nitrogen in practice, putting some at sowing and some later, because that is how I keep the crop feeding steadily instead of wasting fertilizer early.

For water, I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat in my area usually benefits from several timely irrigations, especially around overwinter recovery, jointing, and grain filling if water is available. Maize I will irrigate fewer times and focus on key growth periods. I will not spray pesticides on a fixed calendar just for the sake of spraying, but over a normal year I expect a few applications to control the common diseases, insects, and weeds that would otherwise cut yield. I will keep the rotation clean, use familiar field management, and aim for dependable production rather than chasing risky high yields.
